claims.text: A 19-year-old female presented with sore throat, right-sided jaw pain and a right neck mass present for 4 months. Neck ultrasound showed a markedly vascular mass at the right carotid sheath, and MRI showed an enhancing right carotid space mass with carotid and jugular vein splaying, suggesting a vagal paraganglioma with schwannoma less likely.

evidence.quote: A 19-year-old female presented with sore throat, right-sided jaw pain and a right neck mass that had been present for the past 4 months.
A neck ultrasound scan showed a markedly vascular mass in relation to the right carotid sheath.
MRI showed an enhancing mass in the right carotid space near the bifurcation, extending superiorly to within 1 cm of the skull base.
Characteristic splaying of the carotid artery and internal jugular vein (Figure 1)

claims.text: Enlarged jugular chain and retropharyngeal nodes were felt likely reactive, urinary catecholamines were normal and abdominal MRI showed no adrenal or extra-adrenal paraganglioma. At surgery hypervascular solid nodes were seen in levels 2 and 3, and frozen section showed paraganglioma cells in them, confirming malignancy.
